post: Students have a part to play in their communities long before they graduate. Teachers help them see where to begin. At the National Forum to Advance Rural Education in San Antonio, BRI's Rachel Humphries, Senior Director of Civic Learning, and Gerald Gangaram, Vice President of Student Programs, led a session on how rural schools can connect civics instruction with opportunities for students to contribute to their communities. Thank you to Mark Conlon, PhD, BRI Master Teacher Christian Wrabley, and the National Rural Education Association. Were grateful to the educators helping students build the knowledge and confidence to take part in civic life. Let's bring civics to life together:  https://bit.ly/48aACzX  #RuralEdForum  #CivicEducation

Congratulations to Rachel Morrison, the Bill of Rights Institute's National Civics Teacher of the Year for the 2026-2027 school year! Rachel's students help preserve veterans' stories. They also help lead the project that makes those connections possible. Through the GHS Veterans Project, which she founded, senior interns organize events, speak to community groups, and interview future interns. Rachel gives students real responsibility for work that connects their school and community. Meet the teacher helping students put civic responsibility into practice:  https://bit.ly/4hYzdm8 Goochland County Public Schools

Jordan Gray's eighth graders not only study how laws are made, they also debate which ones should pass. Through classroom lawmaking simulations, he gives students practice thinking through decisions together. His goal: students who can ask tough questions, listen to people they disagree with, and reach their own informed conclusions. Congratulations, Jordan, one of the 10 finalists for the Bill of Rights Institute's National Civics Teacher of the Year Award! Meet Jordan:  https://bit.ly/3WB2dI0  #CivicEducation  #TeacherLeadership

Jaimee Martin's former eighth graders wanted another AP class. She helped them do something about it. Together, they worked with school administrators to add AP Government. Now she teaches it, and her students have firsthand experience turning an idea into action. Congratulations, Jaimee, one of the 10 finalists for the Bill of Rights Institutes National Civics Teacher of the Year Award! Meet the teacher helping students put their ideas to work:  https://bit.ly/4818sY9  #CivicEducation  #TeacherLeadership

These students brought not only their civic knowledge to the national stage, they also brought ideas for their communities. Congratulations to the 2026 National Civics Bees top finishers: champion Peter Daniell of Colorado, second-place winner Araoluwakiitan Afolabi of Florida, and third-place winner Carolyn Taylor of Michigan. Together with their fellow finalists, they put their knowledge, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills to the test. BRI was proud to serve again as the official content partner of the National Civics Bee. Our work with the Bee has included study guides, competition questions, and educator resources that connect civic learning with the skills of citizenship. For us, the purpose extends well beyond the competition: helping students understand our founding principles, think for themselves, and prepare to contribute to our nation. Thank you to the U. S. Chamber of Commerce Foundation and its initiative, the Civic Trust, for bringing these young voices together. Meet the winners and explore the championship highlights:  https://bit.ly/4inmUQe  #NationalCivicsBee  #CivicEducation Photo credit: U. S. Chamber of Commerce Foundation

Lawtnee Frazier isnt looking for a classroom full of matching opinions. When her eighth graders consider whether Andrew Jackson should stay on the $20 bill, they study his presidency and support their answers with evidence. Some argue for keeping him; others want a replacement. What matters is how they make their case. Congratulations, Lawtnee, one of the 10 finalists for the Bill of Rights Institutes National Civics Teacher of the Year Award! Meet the Quail Hollow Middle School teacher helping students think for themselves:  https://bit.ly/4jln8IE  #CivicEducation  #TeacherLeadership

Christopher Klugman used to receive students' letters in a legislators office. Now he helps students write them. At BASIS Scottsdale in Arizona, his students study the Constitution, develop arguments, and write to elected officials. They're learning how to make a case and take part in civic life. Congratulations, Christopher, one of the 10 finalists for the Bill of Rights Institute's National Civics Teacher of the Year Award! Meet Christopher:  https://bit.ly/3VR2S7Y  #CivicEducation  #TeacherLeadership

Here's the part of the Civic Star Challenge that surprises people: Winners are selected by drawing. That means there's no panel scoring your teaching. No rubric. No one deciding whether your lesson was impressive enough. You share a real classroom moment, and you're in the drawing for $5,000. The ones who don't win are the ones who don't enter. Share your story today:  https://bit.ly/45xK27C  #CivicStarChallenge  #TeacherLife

Alishia Gaston Stack asks her students to propose a 28th Amendment. Then comes the challenge: making the case for it. At Lowndes High School in Valdosta, Georgia, students research their proposals, weigh the pros and cons, and present to classmates acting as Congress. They have to think beyond what they want changed to explain why it belongs in the Constitution. Congratulations, Alishia, one of the 10 finalists for the Bill of Rights Institutes National Civics Teacher of the Year Award! Meet the teacher helping students turn opinions into reasoned arguments:  https://bit.ly/4zy9LcY  #CivicEducation  #TeacherLeadership

Monica Brown puts an important decision in her fourth graders hands: how will they help their community? At Oakshire Elementary School in Memphis, students investigate local needs, choose a service project, and carry it out with help from family and community members. They get practice making thoughtful decisions and taking responsibility for what happens next. Congratulations, Monica, one of the 10 finalists for the Bill of Rights Institutes National Civics Teacher of the Year Award! Meet the teacher helping young students put civic responsibility into practice:  https://lnkd.in/e_4GMnp7  #CivicEducation  #TeacherLeadership
